plan_a_advantages: More emphasis on aerobic base building.
Lower overall volume of high-intensity sessions.
plan_b_advantages: Includes a dedicated strength training session.
Long run is longer, potentially building more overall endurance (though riskier).
More focused on specific speed work (intervals).
More structured and potentially more motivating due to the inclusion of varied session types.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it prioritizes building a solid aerobic base with a lower volume of high-intensity work. While Plan B includes more intense sessions (tempo, intervals, strength), it does so with minimal recovery and a longer, more demanding long run, which could lead to overtraining and hinder progress. Plan A’s consistent, lower-impact aerobic work, combined with a single, strategically placed tempo run, is a more sustainable approach for developing the endurance needed for faster trail running. Furthermore, the inclusion of cross-training days in Plan A provides valuable recovery and reduces the risk of overuse injuries.
